authority.legal_name: Ras Al Khaimah Transport Authority (RAKTA), Government of Ras Al Khaimah
authority.geography_type: northern emirate with a long Gulf coastline, reclaimed resort islands and waterfront lagoon communities
authority.home_waters_label: Ras Al Khaimah's coast, islands and lagoons

mandate.summary: RAKTA plans and regulates public transport across Ras Al Khaimah — bus, taxi and a developing marine network — under the RAKTA Transport Master Plan 2030. It has begun a Marine Transport Project and is actively piloting new mobility (robobus/robotaxi at Al Marjan, an eVTOL MOU with Skyports).
current_priorities: Deliver the RAKTA Transport Master Plan 2030 (bus expansion, new routes, marine project)
Stand up the Marine Transport Project (Phase 1 heritage abra along the creek)
Serve the fast-growing Al Marjan Island / Wynn integrated-resort district (opening 2027)
Pilot advanced, clean mobility (autonomous shuttles, eVTOL) and decarbonize under UAE Net Zero 2050

policy_targets.vision: RAKTA Transport Master Plan 2030; UAE Net Zero 2050

marine_status.marine_project_phase1: Heritage Abra service introduced along the Ras Al Khaimah creek/corniche (first phase of the Marine Transport Project)
marine_status.al_marjan_link: Classic Taxi routes within Al Marjan Island connecting Al Qawasim Corniche
marine_status.innovation: Robobus/robotaxi trials on Al Marjan Island; eVTOL MOU with RAKTDA + Skyports
marine_status.demand_driver: Wynn Al Marjan Island integrated resort (opening 2027) and the Mina Al Arab / Al Hamra waterfront communities

policy_targets.relevance: RAK's marine network is at its start, and a wave of waterfront demand is arriving with Al Marjan/Wynn. A zero-emission foiling tier lets RAKTA leapfrog straight to a clean, fast public water network connecting the resort islands, the lagoon communities and the city corniche — fully aligned to Net Zero 2050 and RAK's appetite for advanced mobility.

precedent.headline: RAKTA has already started on the water — and is building one of the region's fastest-growing waterfront destinations.

existing_marine_network.modes: Heritage Abra (Marine Transport Project Phase 1); Classic Taxi linking Al Marjan and the corniche
existing_marine_network.note: The authority has explicitly opened a marine workstream and is connecting Al Marjan Island to the city — the natural backbone for a fast public water network.

demand_corridor.link: Al Marjan Island / Wynn <-> Al Hamra <-> Mina Al Arab <-> RAK city corniche
demand_corridor.stat: A ~30 km coastal string of resort islands and lagoon communities served today only by congested coastal road
demand_corridor.relevance: A clean, fast water spine along this string is exactly the kind of high-value, tourism-and-resident corridor RAK is investing in.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier lets RAKTA stand up a clean public water network from the start rather than retrofitting a diesel fleet. Foiling hulls are fast, near-silent and low-wake — ideal for the reclaimed-island breakwaters and shallow lagoons of Al Marjan, Mina Al Arab and Al Hamra — and they fit RAK's clear appetite for advanced, autonomous-ready mobility.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real berths/marinas during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Network strings the resort islands, lagoon communities and the city corniche.

boarding_points.name: Wynn Al Marjan Island arrival lagoon
Ras Al Khaimah Creek / Old Town

domestic_pairs.rationale: The two flagship resort/marina districts; today a coastal road loop. Anchor corridor.
Al Hamra to the Mina Al Arab lagoon community; short coastal hop.
Lagoon community to the city corniche core; relieves the coastal road into RAK city.
Full-length resort-island-to-city water spine (mirrors the Classic Taxi road link, on water).
Heritage creek (Marine Project Phase 1) to the Jazirat Al Hamra heritage waterfront.
Resort island to the heritage village waterfront; tourism corridor.

regional_links.note: Secondary and clearly optional. The Al Marjan <-> Dubai Islands leg is DOMESTIC within the UAE. Cross-border legs (Musandam/Oman) are out of the core proposal.

links.note: Within-UAE express linking the Al Marjan resort district to Dubai's northern waterfront; long-range (Quanta-LR class), optional after the RAK coastal spine is proven.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic and regional leg must be routed through navigable open water and dredged channels with NO land crossings. Hand-curated waypoints required wherever reclaimed-island breakwaters, lagoon entrances, the commercial port TSS or northern reef flats would otherwise be clipped.

hazards.detail: Al Marjan is reclaimed (coral-shaped fronds) enclosed by breakwaters; route around the outer breakwater through the marked openings, never across the fronds or land.

hazards.hazard: Mina Al Arab & Al Hamra lagoons
hazards.detail: These are dredged lagoon communities; snap entries to the channel mouths and keep geometry in charted channels, not across the shallow lagoon flats.
Saqr Port is a major bulk-cargo port north of the city; keep all geometry clear of its traffic separation scheme and approaches.
The creek mouth and the northern coast carry shallow reef/sand flats; follow charted channels and hand-waypoint around the flats.

hazards.hazard: Al Marjan <-> Dubai offshore (optional link only)
hazards.detail: If routed, keep the line in open Gulf water clear of the Saqr Port and Dubai (Hamriyah/Dubai Islands) approaches and any reclamation; hand-waypoint the full leg.
